# Claude Code prompt: improvement track with several modules, due dates, feedback and auto-generation

Paste everything below the line into Claude Code at the repo root.

---

**Task.** Today the app generates only one audio lesson for an improvement track. Build **a track of several modules**, each with its own **due date**, where **only the next module is generated at any time**:

1. When a track starts, a plan of modules is created (titles and due dates), and **Module 1 is generated at once**.
2. The teacher downloads the audio, uses it in class, and **gives feedback**. Then she presses **Get the next module**.
3. If she gives **no feedback**, the next module is **generated automatically on its due date**, and silence is never read as success.
4. The number of modules depends on the error and on the feedback, up to a cap.

**New word.** Everywhere a teacher or coach sees it, the word **lesson** becomes **module**. Examples: Module 2 of 4, Get the next module, Download audio, Audio module. Drafts for Seema to review: Hindi मॉड्यूल, Tamil தொகுதி. Keep internal code names unless a rename is trivial and safe. Do not edit any deck.

## Rules

- **Code decides which module comes next. The AI only words it.** The branch table in Step 3 is a pure function with tests.
- **Silence is never scored.** No feedback means the planned next module is generated, and the record says so.
- **Idempotent.** A double press, a repeated job run or a retry can never create two copies of the same module.
- **Text first.** Audio is made only when the teacher presses Download audio, through the existing speech layer (Bodhan first and Sarvam as fallback, if built).
- **Counts only for coaches and officers.** A teacher sees her own track. No names anywhere.
- **Content comes from the approved library first.** Anything you write yourself is marked `status: draft` with `TODO-HUMAN(Seema): review`, shown to teachers with a Draft label (and the existing Demo: pre-approved badge in judge mode). List every new text in the report.
- Follow `docs/design/stitch/DESIGN.md`, 44 px targets, every string in `en`, `hi` and `ta`, and text that fits in Hindi and Tamil.
- **Never delete or weaken a test.** Work on a branch and make no push or merge to the evaluated version.

## Step 0. Read first, and find why there is only one

Read `CLAUDE.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `PROGRESS.md`, `AI_USAGE.md`, `docs/design/stitch/DESIGN.md`, and the code for: track and cohort start, the track rule, call 5 and the lesson content, `services/cohort_run/next_lesson.py` (it already chooses a next lesson from feedback), the feedback card, the lesson player and download, the review queue, any scheduler or background job, the speech layer, the cohort and coach pages, and the end-to-end tests.

Before changing anything, **write down why only one lesson is generated today**, with file and line evidence: is it the content library (one lesson per error), the track start, a missing plan, a missing trigger, or the UI? Then write what already exists and can be reused. Put this at the top of the report.

## Step 1. Data model

Add or extend, with a migration:

- `track`: id, cohort id, teacher id (one track per teacher), error code, start date, planned end date (the next check date), status (active, completed, stopped), cap on modules.
- `track_module`: id, track id, **number**, template id, approach id, title, **due date**, status, generated at, generated by (`start`, `teacher`, `due_date`, `coach`), branch (`first`, `tried`, `partly`, `not_yet`, `no_feedback`), a human-readable **reason**, the text, the audio reference, the language. **A unique constraint on (track id, number).**
- `module_feedback`: module id, answer (`tried`, `partly`, `not_yet`), a masked optional note, time given.
- `module_event`: module id, event, time, actor role (an audit and log record).

Statuses of a module: `planned`, `ready`, `downloaded`, `feedback_given`, `completed`, `skipped`, `expired`. Define the legal transitions in one place and test them.

## Step 2. The content library: ordered modules and alternatives

In `content/`, each error code gets a **module plan**: an ordered list of module templates, for example 3 or 4, each with an approach id, a title, a short purpose, the text sections (what to do, steps, materials, how to know it worked) and its source label. Each template also lists **alternative approaches** for the branch not yet and a **smaller-step version** for the branch partly.

- Reuse what exists first. If the library has only one lesson per error, extend its schema, split or extend it into an ordered plan, and mark every new or changed text as a draft.
- A track for an error with no plan keeps today's single module and says so in the log. Never invent content silently.
- Hindi and Tamil text where it exists. Where a language version is missing, show English with a note, and do not machine-translate here.

## Step 3. The branch function (pure code)

`next_module(plan, history, previous_feedback, cap) -> NextModule(template, branch, reason, stop?)`.

| Feedback on the previous module | Next module |
| --- | --- |
| tried | The next module in the plan |
| partly | The same approach as a smaller step, with more practice, then rejoin the plan |
| not yet | A different approach from the library for the same error, skipping approaches already tried |
| none by the due date | The planned next module. Silence is never read as tried |

Rules: never repeat an approach already used unless the branch is partly. Respect the cap (default 6 modules in total, configurable). When the cap is reached, or the plan and its alternatives run out, return `stop` with the message Talk to your mentor or coach, which is a person, and notify the coach. Stop planning at the track's end date (the next check). The reason string is built from fixed templates in `en`, `hi` and `ta`, for example: Module 3 is a different approach because you told us Module 2 is not yet working.

## Step 4. Starting a track

When a track starts (a cohort starts, or a teacher starts her own, or the single-class cohort):

- Create the plan: Module 1 to N with title and **due date**, where N is the planned length (the plan's default, within the cap). Due dates default to 7 days apart from the start (config `MODULE_GAP_DAYS`), skipping no days by default. They are the dates when a module is generated automatically if it was not generated earlier.
- **Generate Module 1 immediately**: assemble the text from the library in code (optionally worded by call 5, with coach review as today), and make it available.
- Modules after the first stay `planned`, showing only their title and due date. No content is generated for them yet.

## Step 5. Generating a module

One function, `generate_module(track, number, trigger)`, used by every trigger:

- Takes a database lock (or uses the unique constraint with a transaction) so only one run wins. A second call returns the existing module without error.
- Chooses the branch with `next_module`, assembles the text in code from the library, and stores the reason. If AI wording is switched on, call 5 words it from approved material, and it goes to the coach's review queue. If nobody has approved it by the due date, **release the library wording** (the plain approved text).
- Caches the text and later the audio by (template, branch, language), not by teacher, so teachers with the same branch share one audio file.
- Records a `module_event` with the trigger and reason.

## Step 6. The two triggers

1. **The teacher presses Get the next module.** It is enabled only after feedback on the current module. Before that it is disabled, with the visible note: Give feedback on Module 2 to get Module 3, or it will arrive on 17 Nov. A coach can also generate a module for a cohort (audited).
2. **A daily job on the due date.** `python tasks.py modules-due`, run every day at **06:00 Indian time** by a scheduler (use what the project already has; otherwise provide a secured endpoint and a Cloud Scheduler example in the docs, and an in-process fallback for development). It finds every planned module whose due date is today or earlier, belonging to an active track, and generates it with the branch no\_feedback, or with the actual branch if feedback exists. It **catches up** if a run was missed. It is idempotent, retries a failure with backoff, and notifies the coach if a module still fails. The clock and the time zone are injectable for tests.

## Step 7. The teacher's screen

On the track page (and as a card on Home):

- A **timeline** of modules: Module 1 of 4 is the current one, with a status chip and an icon and word (never colour alone); later modules show their title and due date only.
- The **current module card**: the text first and collapsible, **Download audio**, a **Why this module?** line from the record, and the **feedback card** (Tried, Partly, Not yet, and an optional note, with names masked).
- **Get the next module**, with its disabled reason when it is not available.
- Earlier modules stay readable and their audio stays downloadable. Late feedback attaches to its module and only affects modules not yet generated.
- A banner when the cap is reached: Talk to your mentor or coach. When the track ends: It is time for the next check.
- Offline: text and downloaded audio work, and generating a module needs a connection, with the reason shown.

## Step 8. The coach's screen

On the cohort page, per module of the track: how many teachers are at it, how many have downloaded it, how many gave feedback (counts for tried, partly, not yet), overdue items, and failed generations. **Edit due dates** for the cohort, or shift all remaining dates (for a holiday), with an audit entry and a reason. Dates of modules already generated cannot change. Coaches and officers see counts only.

## Step 9. Edge cases to handle and test

Double press and double job; feedback given after the next module was already generated; a teacher who never downloads (flag the coach after N days, configurable); a due date that falls on a day when the app was down; Indian midnight and daylight handling (no daylight saving, but test the 06:00 boundary); the cap; the track end date; a coach moving dates earlier or later; a missing language version; two teachers in one cohort at different modules; a module template deleted from the library after a track began (keep the generated text); and the single-class cohort.

## Step 10. The rename sweep

Search strings (`en.json`, `hi.json`, `ta.json`), help documents, the README, the judge guide's sources and the assistant's reference for user-facing uses of lesson. Change them to module in the three languages. Leave internal names (files, tables, functions) unless a rename is trivial. Write a list of the places in the decks and the video script that still say lesson, **and do not edit them**.

## Step 11. Tests

- **Pure logic:** the branch table for each feedback value and for none, no repeat of an approach, the cap and stop, the end date, and the reason strings in three languages.
- **State machine:** every legal and illegal transition.
- **Idempotency:** two simultaneous presses and two simultaneous job runs create one module.
- **The daily job with a frozen clock:** a due module is generated with no\_feedback, a module with feedback uses its real branch, a missed day is caught up, and it runs correctly across the 06:00 Indian time boundary.
- **End to end** (fake clock, recorded AI, mock speech): a three-module track: Module 1 at start, feedback tried, the teacher gets Module 2, no feedback on Module 2, the job generates Module 3 on its date with no\_feedback, the coach edits a date, and the timeline and coach counts are right.
- **Roles:** a teacher sees only her track, and coaches and officers see counts.
- **Screens:** the timeline, the disabled reason text, the cap banner, offline behaviour, axe, and Hindi and Tamil fit at 360 px.
- Existing suites still pass. Report the counts before and after.

## Step 12. Report and docs

`docs/build/reports/MODULES.md`: why there was one lesson before, what was reused, what was built, the branch table, the content gaps and every new text for Seema to review, the scheduler setup, and the tests. Update `docs/help/teacher.md` and the coach help, the README, `docs/RUBRIC_MAP.md`, `AI_USAGE.md` and `DECISIONS.md` (entry dated today), and add the new screens to `docs/design/stitch/INVENTORY.md`.

**Order:** Step 0, then Steps 1 to 3 with unit tests, then Steps 4 to 6, then Steps 7 and 8, then Steps 9 to 12.

**Done when** a track plans several modules with due dates and generates only the first, feedback leads to the right next module through the branch table, an unanswered module is generated on its due date by the daily job without feedback, no module can be created twice, teachers and coaches see the timeline and counts, the word module replaces lesson in every user-facing string, and the tests and report are done.
